newsitem.title: USA: Spot US propane prices soar on cold forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Spot US propane prices soar on cold forecasts.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices soared in trade on Friday as players kept a close eye on weather forecasts predicting cold weather, traders said.
Volume, however, remained light amid continuing volatility in the market and a limited number of players due to an industry holiday event that began late yesterday.
Players added, though, that there was one large Canadian producer buying barrels ahead of the cold weather, expected to reach the Midwest next week.
"It's basically one producer and trader to trader deals that are pushing prices up," said one Houston player.
In the Midwest, Conway, Kansas, hub traded between 93.00 cents and 93.50 cents a gallon, 8.00 cents above Thursday's levels.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot material also rose in line with Conway, moving up about 4.00 cents to 61.00/61.75 cents.
Focus remained on propane, with the other liquidified petroleum gases idling at somewhat steady levels.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1631
